results.name: legacy

findings.message: hostPath volume "scratch": its data is lost with the node
findings.remediation:
Use emptyDir for scratch data, or a PersistentVolumeClaim for data that must outlive the node.

# spec.template.spec.volumes
- name: scratch
  emptyDir: {}

findings.message: no topology spread or pod anti-affinity: replicas can land on the same node or zone
findings.remediation:
Spread the replicas across zones and nodes.

# spec.template.spec
topologySpreadConstraints:
  - maxSkew: 1
    topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
    whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
    labelSelector:
      matchLabels:
        app: legacy
  - maxSkew: 1
    topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
    whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
    labelSelector:
      matchLabels:
        app: legacy

findings.message: no PodDisruptionBudget: draining can remove too many replicas at once
findings.remediation:
Add a PodDisruptionBudget so a drain removes one replica at a time.

apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: legacy
  namespace: shop
spec:
  maxUnavailable: 1
  unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy: AlwaysAllow
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: legacy

findings.message: container "legacy" has no readinessProbe: traffic can reach a pod that is not ready
findings.remediation:
Add a readinessProbe so traffic only reaches pods that can serve it. Point it at your health endpoint.

# spec.template.spec.containers[legacy]
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /healthz
    port: 8080
  periodSeconds: 5
  failureThreshold: 3

findings.message: no preStop hook: in-flight requests may be cut when the node is reclaimed
findings.remediation:
Add a short preStop sleep so the endpoint is removed from load balancers before the process gets SIGTERM.

# spec.template.spec.containers[legacy]
lifecycle:
  preStop:
    exec:
      command: ["sleep", "15"]

confidenceReasons: node-local data in a hostPath volume

results.name: import

findings.message: backoffLimit is 0: a single lost pod fails the whole job
findings.remediation:
Let the job retry: with backoffLimit 0 one lost pod fails it.

# spec
backoffLimit: 6

findings.message: no podFailurePolicy that ignores DisruptionTarget: a pod lost to an interruption can count against backoffLimit
findings.remediation:
Do not count pods lost to a node disruption against backoffLimit (needs restartPolicy: Never).

# spec
podFailurePolicy:
  rules:
    - action: Ignore
      onPodConditions:
        - type: DisruptionTarget

findings.message: progress is lost on interruption unless the job checkpoints; the tool cannot verify that
findings.remediation: Write progress to durable storage (S3, a PVC) and resume from it when the job starts, so an interruption does not restart from zero.

confidenceReasons: job: whether it checkpoints its progress cannot be verified

warnings: All 3 pods run on one node (spot-readiness-it-control-plane): losing it takes the whole workload down.
3 pods run on Spot nodes that are all m5.large: one capacity shortage in that pool interrupts them together.

findings.message: supports only one Availability Zone: that zone running out of Spot capacity leaves the pool without nodes
findings.remediation:
Let the NodePool use every zone that has a subnet, or list at least two.

# NodePool spec.template.spec.requirements
- key: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
  operator: In
  values: ["<zone-a>", "<zone-b>", "<zone-c>"]

findings.message: allows only 2 instance families (at least 3 recommended)
findings.remediation:
Allow several instance categories and make Karpenter keep a minimum of families.

# NodePool spec.template.spec.requirements
- key: karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-category
  operator: In
  values: ["c", "m", "r"]
- key: karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-family
  operator: Exists
  minValues: 5

findings.message: allows only 4 instance types (AWS recommends at least 10 for Spot)
findings.remediation:
List more instance types, or better, constrain by category and generation and let Karpenter pick the types.

# NodePool spec.template.spec.requirements
- key: karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-category
  operator: In
  values: ["c", "m", "r"]
- key: karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-generation
  operator: Gt
  values: ["2"]
- key: node.kubernetes.io/instance-type
  operator: Exists
  minValues: 10

findings.message: no explicit disruption budget: Karpenter applies its default of 10% of nodes at a time
findings.remediation:
Set a disruption budget that fits you. Remove a budget of 0 nodes that is always active, or limit it with a schedule.

# NodePool spec.disruption
budgets:
  - nodes: "10%"
  - nodes: "0"          # block voluntary disruption only during business hours
    schedule: "0 9 * * mon-fri"
    duration: 8h

findings.message: no minValues on instance type, family or category: nothing makes Karpenter keep a minimum of instance diversity
findings.remediation:
Make Karpenter keep a minimum of instance diversity.

# NodePool spec.template.spec.requirements
- key: karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-family
  operator: Exists
  minValues: 5
